about.description: The How to play screen: the goal, and the main moves.

actions.description: Things a button or key can do.

hints.description: Hints, a line in the panel while their conditions hold.

name_entry.description: Typing the name for a high score with a pad: `text_entry`'s keys, for a second card.

pad.description: What a pad does, by state (`default` for every state).

situations.description: How a crafted situation enters play.

states.description: Moments of the game, checked in order.

text_entry.description: Typing a word the game asks for, with a pad.

values.description: Named facts about the game's memory.

About.description:
`[about]`: the How to play screen, shown when a game starts: the game's goal, and how its
main moves are made.

goal.description: What the game is about, in a sentence or two.

Action.description: `[[actions]]`: something a button or key does beyond a key or a direction.

host_key.description: A key the Spectrum doesn't have that also does it.

joystick.description: Joystick directions or fire held while it lasts.

menu.description: Its row in the guidance menu, in these words ("End this game"); wants a second press.

menu_in.description: The states in which the menu offers it; every state when left out.

patch_for_frame.description: Patches applied while it lasts, then undone.

script.description: A function of the script to call.

sequence.description: Keys tapped one after another, each for `frames` frames with as many between.

Add.description: Where a kept list's entries come from.

anyOf.description: A value read while the game is in a state.

Address.description: A 16-bit address: a number from 0 to 65535, or a "0x" hex string.

Amount.description: A number, or a value's full amount.

Border.description: How much of the border round the screen is shown.

oneOf.description: None: the game draws nothing there, so the screen alone is shown, larger.

Bytes.description: Bytes in hex, separated by spaces: "CD 40 75".

Charset.description: How a `text` value's codes map to letters.

anyOf.description: A table of the game's own.

first.description: The code of the first letter in `chars`.

call.description:
A routine of the game's called once, at the next sync point in play after it goes on,
returning to the sync address: one that redraws what `set` changed.

hold.description: Values that may not go down while it's on.

marks_score.description: Whether a game played with it on is a training game.

set.description: Values written at each sync point while it's on.

Column.description: Where a widget goes in the panel.

oneOf.description: The panel's whole width, below everything in the columns above it.

Count.description: How many: a number, or the value that holds it.

DirectionKeys.description: A game's own keys for the joystick's directions and fire.

Field.description: A field of a table's records, or of a high-score entry.

bits.description: Only these bits: true when they're set.

charset.description: For `text`: how codes map to letters.

len.description: Its length, for the multi-byte types.

type.description: What kind of value it is.

id.description: Unique, lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`: names the data folder and the file.

notice.description: Replaces the standard "not affiliated" notice; keep its meaning.

title.description: In plain text, as the game is known.

stride.description: Bytes from one entry to the next.

title.description: The table's heading in the panel after a game: the game's own name for it.

Hint.description: One thing to press, and what it does.

keys.description: The keyboard's key as shown (`"Alt"`), or arrows (`"← ↑ → ↓"`).

pad.description: The pad part that does it, by position: `west`, `dpad`…

HowTo.description: `[[about.how]]`: one of the main moves, with what does it.

keys.description:
The keyboard's key as shown, when not the one worked out from `pad`; arrows are shown
bare (`"← →"`).

pad.description:
The pad part that does it, by position (`east`, `dpad`…): its button shows while a pad
is plugged in, and the keyboard's key for it, worked out from the `[pad]` mapping in
play, always.

oneOf.description: The game's own keys, named in `[run] keys`.

Keyboard.description: What the computer's keyboard is in play.

oneOf.description:
A pad, through `[pad]`: the arrows and WASD its D-pad, Space its west button, Enter its
Start. No Spectrum key reaches the game.
The Spectrum's own keyboard: its keys reach the game, and the arrows are still the D-pad.

Layout.description: The order of a picture's bytes.

oneOf.description: Row by row, top to bottom, each row left to right.

In 8 × 8 character cells, left to right then top to bottom, each cell's eight rows in
turn, as the screen's characters are drawn.

description.description: What it adds, in a line.

Machine.description: The Spectrum a game runs on.

MarkerPlace.description: Where in its cell a map's marker sits.

MarkerShape.description: A shape the map draws a marker as.

oneOf.description: Where the player is: an outline round its cell.
The marker's own picture, from the widget's `pictures`.
The marker's `label`, a few characters: a door's number.
A mask byte before each byte.

download.description: Where the player can get it legally.

files.description: File names it's distributed under, matched in any case.

name.description: How the tape prompt names the dump.

sha1.description: The SHA-1 of the tape file itself (not a zip around it), 40 hex digits.

Notice.description: What a card over the picture says: a line, and hints along its bottom.

heading.description:
Its heading, when not the program's own ("Paused" for the pause, "How it plays" for
the title).

hints.description: What to press, along the bottom.

text.description: The line: "Move or fire to go on."

OneOrMany.description: One of something, or a list of them.

OneOrMany2.description: One of something, or a list of them.

OneOrMany3.description: One of something, or a list of them.

Pad.description: `[pad.*]`: what each part of a pad does in a state (`default` for all states).

any.description:
In a state's own table: what every other part does there (Select apart), and every
other key of the keyboard while it plays as a pad (Esc, the F keys and the modifiers
apart).

PadTable.description: Keys, a tap, or an action.

frames.description: How many frames a tap lasts.

keys.description: Keys held as long as the button is.

sequence.description: Keys tapped one after another, each for `frames` frames with as many between.

tap.description: Keys pressed for `frames` frames, however long the button is held.

PadTarget.description: What a part of a pad does.

anyOf.description: Keys, a tap, or an action.

PanelHint.description:
`[[hints]]`: a line in the panel, under the level's name, while its conditions hold. Of
those that hold at the guidance level, the one with the lowest `priority` shows.

for_seconds.description:
Shows for this many seconds of holding, then not again until its condition (its
`when` and `script`, or its `state` when it gives neither) has stopped holding.

from_level.description: The guidance level from which it shows: 1 or more.

priority.description: Which shows when several hold: 1 before 2; in the order listed when equal.

script.description: Holds only while the script names this condition in the `hints` it returns.

state.description: Holds only while the game is in one of these states.

text.description: What it says: one short line.

to_level.description: The highest level it shows at, when not every level above `from_level`.

when.description: Holds only while this test of a value holds.

Patch.description: Bytes written over the game's, checked first.

bank.description: On a 128K, the RAM bank for an address from 0xC000.

expect.description: The bytes that must be there first.

file.description: Its file in the game's data folder.

label.description: What the list holds, for "Forget the …".

most.description: The most entries it keeps: past that, the oldest go first.

Role.description: What a state means to the program. At most one state has each.

oneOf.description: The title screen: the kept high scores go in, and a game in hand ends.

A game being played: training switches apply, a game's record starts, and a crafted
situation enters.
Paused: the picture dims, and the notice shows.
Game over: no game is under way.

border.description: How much of the border is shown once the tape has loaded.

hold_loading_screen.description: Whether the loading screen stays until a key is pressed.

joystick.description: What the pad's directions drive in play.

keyboard.description: What the computer's keyboard is in play: a pad, or the Spectrum's own keyboard.

keyboard_in.description:
With `keyboard = "spectrum"`: the states it's the Spectrum's keyboard in, a pad in the
rest. Empty, it's the Spectrum's throughout.

keys.description: With `joystick = "keys"`: the game's own keys for each direction and fire.

sync.description: The top of the game's main loop, reached once per frame of play.

file.description: Its file, within the definition's folder or zip.

Set.description: A value to set, and what to.

Situations.description: `[situations]`: how a crafted situation enters play.

enter.description: The routine that starts play in the current room.

start.description:
The keys that take the game from its loaded tape to play, in turn: each tapped a
second after the game's state last changed, and again every forty seconds while it
stays.

State.description: `[[states]]`: a moment of the game. The first that matches is the game's state.

notice.description: For the `paused` and `title` roles: what the notice over the picture says.

pc.description: Matches if the processor executed one of these during the frame.

role.description: What it means to the program, if anything.

set.description:
Values written at each sync point while the game is in this state: a choice the
program makes for the player, such as the joystick on a title.

when.description: Matches if this test of a value holds.

Test.description: A test of a value, or a combination of tests.

TextEntry.description: `[text_entry]` and `[name_entry]`: typing a word the game asks for, with a pad.

card_row.description: The character row the card's top sits at.

choices.description: The kept list offered as choices.

choices_from_level.description: The guidance level from which choices are offered.

key_down_frames.description: Frames each letter's key is held.

key_up_frames.description: Frames between letters, with no key held.

state.description: The state in which the game asks.

Value.description: `[values.*]`: a named fact about the game's memory.

bank.description: On a 128K, the RAM bank (0–7) for an address from 0xC000.

charset.description: For `text`: how codes map to letters.

colors.description: For sprites: a value giving each picture's ink.

count.description: For tables, fonts and sprites: how many there are, or the value that says.

first.description: For fonts: the code of the first character.

height.description: For fonts and sprites: the height in pixels.

layout.description: For sprites: the order of their bytes.

len.description: Its length in bytes, for the multi-byte types.

mask.description: For sprites: where their masks are.

max.description: Its full amount, for meters and cheats that fill it.

stride.description: For tables and sprites: bytes from one to the next.

type.description: What kind of value it is.

width.description: For fonts and sprites: the width in pixels.

writable.description: Whether cheats, scripts and crafted situations may write it.

zero.description: For `digits`: the code of the digit 0 (0x30 when not given).

ValueType.description: What kind of value a value is.

oneOf.description: `len` bytes, one digit each, counting from `zero`.
`len` bytes of bits; bit 0 of the first byte is item 0.

column.description: Where in the panel it goes.

empty.description: What it says when there's nothing to show.

font.description: A `font` value its words are drawn in.

from_level.description: The guidance level from which it shows.

markers.description: For `map-grid`: the shape each kind of marker the script uses is drawn as.

pictures.description: A `sprites` value its pictures come from.

places.description:
For `map-grid`: where in its cell each kind of marker sits, unless a marker says its
own place (`at`); in the middle when a kind isn't listed.

oneOf.description: Short words in the game's font.
Groups of pictures, each dim until answered.
Places on a grid, with walls, markers and routes.
